question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution gives equality before the law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14**

 
 
• Article 14 of the Indian Constitution is about '**Equality Before Law**' and it states:
 
• "The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the** territory of India**."
 
• This article is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution of India, which talks about** Rights to Equality**.
 
• The principle of 'Equality before law' is of British origin, while 'Equal protection of the laws' is borrowed from the** Constitution of the United States**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Article
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Article 18
 
 
 
• Article 18 of the Indian Constitution discusses the 'abolition of titles'.
 
• Within this article, it is expressed that the State cannot confer any titles, and citizens of India cannot accept titles from a foreign State.
 
• This Article is integral to the principle of equality that the Constitution of India strongly advocates.
 
• It is meant to preserve and promote the notion of equal recognition and respect for all citizens, irrespective of their socioeconomic status.
 
• However, this does not apply to academic or military distinctions. So, educational and military awards are allowed to be employed and do not come under the purview of Article 18.
 
 
 
 

 Article 20
 
 
 

 
 
• Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides safeguards to individuals with respect to conviction for offences.
 
• It grants three main rights: protection from ex post facto laws, prohibition of double jeopardy, and protection against self-incrimination.
 
• These rights are considered fundamental as they safeguard individual liberties from arbitrary encroachment by the state.
 
 
 
 

 Article 16
 
 
Article 16- Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment. 

 
 
• It assures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prevents the State from any sort of discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them.
 
• This Article also provides the autonomy to the State to grant special provisions for the backward classes, under-represented States, SC & ST for posts under the State.
 
• Local candidates may also be given preference is certain posts. Reservation of posts for people of a certain religion or denomination in a religious or denominational institution will not be deemed illegal.
